summary: A stale search's live feed top-up runs under one overall time budget that also bounds its rate-limit waits and page writes, and returns what it stored when the budget ends; a feed page counts as delivered only after it is stored; and feed page writes take SQLite's write lock up front so concurrent searches on one store queue instead of failing.
reason: Research pipelines call `search --agent` with a hard kill timeout (30s) and run several searches at once against the same store. Without these, eight sequential page fetches could outrun the caller and discard every stored match, a failed write could exit 0 as an empty live search, and a read-then-write deferred transaction lost its write upgrade to SQLITE_BUSY that busy_timeout cannot wait out.
validated_outcome: Each new test fails without its fix: four store handles writing overlapping feed pages concurrently hit SQLITE_BUSY under the deferred transaction and pass with BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
